description: Single-panel grouped bar chart with a line overlay, plotting yield strength versus alloy number. The y-axis is labelled "Yield strength (MPa)" and is scaled 0-600 in 100 MPa increments; the x-axis is labelled "Alloys" with integer categories 1-5. A key printed above the plot reads "Steels (wt.%): 1 = 7Al-0.002C-0.01Ti; 2 = 7Al-0.004C-0.02Nb; 3 = 8Al-0.003C-0.01Ti-0.01Nb; 4 = 7.5Al-0.004C-0.02Nb; 5 = 6.5Al-0.005C-0.01Ti-0.01Nb". The in-plot legend defines the white bar as "YS (Pre-BH)", the pink bar as "YS (Post-BH)" and the blue filled-circle line as "ΔYS". For every alloy the pink post-BH bar is taller than the paired white pre-BH bar: alloys 1 and 5 have pre-BH tops between the 300 and 400 MPa gridlines and post-BH tops slightly above 400 MPa; alloys 3 and 4 are stronger, alloy 3 being the tallest (pre-BH just above 400 MPa, post-BH approaching 500 MPa). The ΔYS line is essentially flat across all five alloys, lying just below the 100 MPa gridline. No numeric data labels are printed on any bar. The figure demonstrates that the paint-baking treatment (2% deformation + 170°C, 20 min, per caption) raises YS by a near-constant increment in all five Fe-Al ferritic steels.

observations.observation: The y-axis is labelled 'Yield strength (MPa)' and spans 0-600 with major gridlines/tick marks every 100 MPa; the x-axis is labelled 'Alloys' with five integer categories 1-5.
The in-plot legend identifies the white bars as 'YS (Pre-BH)', the pink bars as 'YS (Post-BH)' and the blue filled-circle line as 'ΔYS'.

A composition key printed at the top of the figure reads 'Steels (wt.%): 1 = 7Al-0.002C-0.01Ti; 2 = 7Al-0.004C-0.02Nb; 3 = 8Al-0.003C-0.01Ti-0.01Nb; 4 = 7.5Al-0.004C-0.02Nb; 5 = 6.5Al-0.005C-0.01Ti-0.01Nb'.
For each of the five alloys the pink post-BH bar is taller than its paired white pre-BH bar, i.e. yield strength increases after baking for every composition shown.
The blue ΔYS line runs almost horizontally across the plot at a level just below the 100 MPa gridline for all five alloys, indicating a near-constant bake-hardening increment.
Alloy 3 (8Al-0.003C-0.01Ti-0.01Nb) shows the highest bars in the figure: its pre-BH bar rises just above the 400 MPa gridline and its post-BH bar approaches the 500 MPa gridline.
Alloys 1 and 5 have the lowest pre-BH strengths, with bar tops falling between the 300 and 400 MPa gridlines, and post-BH bar tops only slightly above the 400 MPa gridline.
No numeric data labels are printed on the bars or on the ΔYS markers; all bar values must be estimated from the 100 MPa gridlines.
The caption states the bake-hardening (BH) response was measured after a paint baking treatment of 2% deformation plus 170C for 20 min.
The caption states that the figure also shows the pre- and post-BH yield strengths of the alloys, matching the two bar series.

The citing text reports that about 80 MPa of yield strength can be gained through bake hardening in these high-Al-containing steels with a proper alloy design, which is consistent with the flat ΔYS line drawn just below the 100 MPa gridline.
The citing text attributes the bake-hardening effect to locking of dislocations by excess interstitial elements (free C) in the ferritic matrix.

unreadable_items: Exact numerical YS values per alloy are not printed anywhere; bar heights can only be placed relative to the 100 MPa gridlines.
The degree sign in the caption baking temperature is rendered as '170C' (no ° symbol), so the unit is inferred from context.
